A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 19-page Immune paper, including complete Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish matching research content, with differences confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original jailbreak-defense experiments, model-utility measurements, inference timings, and hyperparameter analyses in Section 6, with additional empirical comparisons in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix C, including benchmark comparisons, utility measurements, timings, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C.1 retain identical reward-guided decoding procedures, objectives, components, and implicit-reward variants.

E1.justification: Both versions retain JailbreakV-28K, all 13 MM-SafetyBench categories across Tables 2 and 6, FigStep, visual adversarial attacks, and MM-Vet. Training-data references and evaluated input scenarios also match.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Original, FigStep, AdaShield, and CoCA. Table 7 also retains Qwen-VL+DPO and the same controlled-decoding variants attributed to Mudgal et al. and Chakraborty et al.

E3.justification: Model configurations, decoding defaults, jailbreak judges, metrics, and attack strengths are identical. The timing evaluation still uses 100 prompts, and the Appendix C.1 KL-divergence analysis still uses 218 prompts.

E4.justification: The attack-strength evaluation, Figure 4 sensitivity analysis for k and alpha, Appendix C.1 KL-divergence comparison, and Appendix E qualitative cases are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains three independent responses per query, with any flagged response constituting a successful jailbreak. There are no changes to seed information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match, including Tables 1–7 and the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains LLaVA-1.6 average ASRs of 60.27% for Original, 19.23% for AdaShield, and 2.45% for Immune.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and definitions in Sections 3–5, Theorem 1, and its complete Appendix B proof are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about insufficient training-time safety alignment and Immune improving jailbreak resistance while preserving model utility, supported by mathematical characterization.

C2.justification: The theoretical interpretations, reward-model vulnerability caveat, and empirical explanations match. Both retain the limitations concerning static datasets and the absence of evaluations against dynamic and defense-aware attacks.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, hyperparameters, checkpoint references, baseline prompts, and project-page access information are unchanged. Appendix A retains Python 3.7.4, PyTorch 1.9.0, and two Nvidia RTX A6000 GPUs.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning passages elsewhere, and all 91 reference entries are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp text changes from v3, dated 20 Mar 2025, to v4, dated 31 May 2025. Article prose, terminology, headings, and organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page marginal arXiv stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–7, Tables 1–7, captions, and the research-content layout remain identical; rendered pages 2–19 match exactly.

improvement.justification: The later version preserves the same methods, theory, experimental evidence, explanations, and limitations throughout the main paper and appendices. Updating and slightly repositioning the arXiv stamp does not meaningfully affect clarity, rigor, completeness, or overall paper quality.
